title: You don’t hear sermons about this part much.
paragraphs: You don’t hear sermons about this part much.

Because it’s messy.
Uncomfortable.
Too close to home.

The dysfunction of Jacob’s family isn’t just a story…
—it’s a mirror.
THE FAMILY GOD CHOSE… WAS BROKEN
Open Genesis and don’t sanitize it.
This wasn’t a clean, godly household.

• Deception between brothers
• Favoritism from parents
• Sexual immorality
• Jealousy that turned violent
• Betrayal that sold a brother into slavery
And at the center of it…

A man chosen by God—
but still shaped by manipulation, fear, and control.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God didn’t wait for the family to be healthy before He worked.

Jacob deceived his father.
Jacob stole a blessing.
Jacob played favorites with his wives and children.

Spiritual Diagnosis:
You don’t just sin privately. You pass patterns publicly.
“The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.” — Jeremiah 31:29
What you normalize becomes what others inherit.
FAVORITISM: THE SPARK THAT IGNITED HATE
Jacob loved Joseph more than the others.

The coat wasn’t just clothing.
It was a statement:
“Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children…” — Genesis 37:3

The brothers didn’t just feel hurt…
They felt replaced.
And hurt, when left unchecked, mutates into hatred.
“They hated him and could not speak peaceably to him.” — Genesis 37:4

Silence filled with resentment.
Smiles hiding bitterness.
A family that eats together but is divided within.

First hatred.
Then conspiracy.
Then violence.

Because if the story ended there—
it would just be tragedy.
But God was not absent in the dysfunction.
“You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good…” — Genesis 50:20

Not excusing sin.
Not ignoring evil.
THE REAL ISSUE ISN’T THE FAMILY…
You look at Jacob’s household and think:
But strip away the drama and what do you find?

• Comparison
• Control
• Hidden sin
• Unresolved wounds
• Pride
Here’s the question no one asks:
Why would God choose a family like this?
Because He wasn’t building a legacy on human goodness.
He was revealing the necessity of grace.
“There is none righteous, no, not one.” — Romans 3:10

Not Jacob.
Not his sons.
Not you.
Joseph was betrayed by his brothers.
Jesus was betrayed by His own.

Joseph suffered unjustly…
but became the means of salvation.

Jesus suffered perfectly…
and became eternal salvation.
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
You can keep blaming your past.

Your family.
Your upbringing.
Your wounds.
But dysfunction is not your excuse anymore.
Because the cross interrupts the cycle.
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation…” — 2 Corinthians 5:17

God can work through broken systems—
but He saves individuals.
